She wanted to leave on several occasions, but he threatened to hurt her and slit her throat if she did. She said Lewis and her had an altercation in the parking lot due to her attempting to leave. He then forced her back inside the hotel and punched her 13 times in the head and face. She informed the officer that Lewis forces her to provide a fake name if they have police interaction. She then provided the officer her correct name. She then stated Lewis has battered her before and has informed police, but nothing ever helps because his mother is a judge. She said she has several phones, but only one works, and Lewis took it from her that very same day prior to the officer's arrival, so she couldn't call them. She also showed officers another phone that wasn't working, which Lewis previously told her that he broke. The phone didn't appear damage, but it would not turn on. The woman still refused ambulance services, but continued complaining of severe face and head pain. Illinois court records indicate that he has an extensive criminal history. Will County records indicate he was set a $200,000 bail. However, after two months in jail, the judge ordered Lewis to be released on a $0 bond. A week later, Lewis failed to show up to court and a warrant was issued for his arrest. Then, in November 2023, he was apprehended on the warrant for failing to appear in court. He then remained in jail for two more months until early 2024 when the Illinois Safety Act went into place, requiring most defendants to be released without needing to place a bond. Court records indicate he pled guilty to felony domestic assault and felony assault on an officer that January. He was referred to a diversion program and released from custody. Lewis has promised the court he will come back for drug testing.
